prompt.v: One side of a triangle is extended. The two angles inside, away from it, are 100° and 58°. What is the exterior angle b?

problems.explain: An exterior angle equals the two interior angles far from it, added: 100 + 58 = 158. It makes a straight line with the angle beside it, 22°, so it is 180 − 22; and the triangle’s three angles add to 180, so the far two are 180 − 22 as well. The angle beside it is never part of the sum. So b = 158°.

It makes a straight line with the angle beside it, 49°, so it is 180 − 49; and the triangle’s three angles add to 180, so the far two are 180 − 49 as well. The angle beside it is never part of the sum. So c = 131°.

It makes a straight line with the angle beside it, 55°, so it is 180 − 55; and the triangle’s three angles add to 180, so the far two are 180 − 55 as well. The angle beside it is never part of the sum. So y = 125°.
